notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no hardware backend was run, and no ROS graph, MuJoCo engine or upstream simulator run is claimed. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: task.json says family ros with helper RosDriver, but the card's first model is the MJCF scene crl_humanoid_commons/data/robots/g1_description/scene_crl.xml and the registry card's device plan is a world.sim resource offering cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. A configuration-only RosDriver can publish and subscribe to the upstream ROS 2 topics, but it cannot express the environment step, the reset-to-model-defaults semantics or the integration state hash those classes require. The package therefore uses the SDK's MujocoDriver for the card's first model and records the deviation in facts.md. It does not claim coverage of the upstream ROS 2 topics (remote, monitor, py_control), the elastic_band or restart services, the FSM state switching, the controllers or the hardware packages. The ROS command/observation interface remains NOT COVERED. The card's entry_symbols list is empty, so no Python entry symbol existed to verify; the served model file exists at the pinned commit.

WHAT IT SERVES: the G1 scene as a simulated R0 world.sim at mhs://localhost/crl-humanoid-g1. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}} and writes data.ctrl (29 motor channels), then calls mj_step for every tick; cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed, native_checkpoint). The G1 actuator block sets no ctrlrange, so the bridge derives no per-channel control limit; no Limit is invented and no site-limits.example.json is needed. The joint actuatorfrcrange values are joint force ranges, not actuator ctrl ranges, and are not used as a control envelope. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served because the MuJoCo bridge has no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults; the reset input seed is accepted by the class contract but does not sample a new state. The second and third card models (the Tron1A scene and the G1 robot include) are not separately served.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package-local stand-in mujoco module in fake.py. It parses the same MJCF scene and its include for the free base, the 29 hinge joints, the 29 motor channels, the joint ranges and the option timestep, then integrates a placeholder torque response of each actuated joint. It loads no mesh or texture and computes no inertia, mass matrix, gravity, contact, friction, equality, tendon or actuator dynamics; it does not implement the integration-state snapshot API, so a snapshot uses the bridge's basic time/qpos/qvel/ctrl fallback. The G1 scene sets no option timestep, so the stand-in uses a placeholder MuJoCo library default of 2 ms and the published timestep_ms comes from that fake; the upstream ROS simulator instead overrides the model timestep from its time_step_size parameter (G1SimNode.h:414, g1_sim.yaml:24), which this direct model load does not apply. The fake was not compared with the real MuJoCo engine; the real sim path (the official mujoco module loading the same scene) was not run. Fidelity is F1 for the wire/state contract only, with engine mujoco:g1 scene crl, determinism seeded/seed_control none, realtime_factor 0 and lockstep clock; the gaps list every difference. No safety limit, number or fact is copied from fake.py; its [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation, all 13 facts, the absent ctrlrange envelope, the lockstep latch stop and the stand-in mujoco module against scene_crl.xml, g1_29dof_crl.xml, G1SimNode.h, BaseNode.h and g1_sim.yaml at the pin. The deviation is right (the card's first model is the MJCF scene the repository's G1 simulator loads with mj_loadXML; its ROS 2 graph carries controller, monitor, FSM and hardware traffic), and the scene and model have no default class, ctrlrange or option timestep. Two defects: the fake, a stand-in with no dynamics, published engine mujoco at F1 (rigid-body dynamics with contacts), and five facts said more than their lines (a pelvis accelerometer on 281 outside 277-280, initializeMuJoCo declared on 393 outside 399-414 with its parameter in BaseNode.h, 'hinge' and 'rad', 'under the robot', and a unit not on the line). The reviewer split the fidelity into the class-level F1 contract of the real engine path and an F0 fidelity_by_backend entry for the fake, as in the reviewed humanoid-control, corrected the five facts and added two (BaseNode's time_step_size; crl_humanoid_hardware's rt/lowcmd) in driver.py, made the fidelity case expect F0 on the fake (test_driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the MuJoCo-family warnings and the digest unchanged. The author's notes above still call the fake's fidelity F1. For the human reviewer: Fake-only MuJoCo world at R0: raw ctrl torques on 29 motors with no controller, so the humanoid falls unless a caller supplies torques; reset restores the MJCF defaults. The repository also drives the real Unitree G1 (Unitree SDK2 rt/lowcmd) and LimX Tron1A through crl_humanoid_hardware; that legged-hardware path is out of scope and would be R2 or higher.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): SDK change MHS/changes/MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS.md: a MuJoCo model that gives no actuator a control range is no longer served silently unbounded; the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required, so the endpoint refuses a step that sets it (MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET, before the native step) until the site's overlay bounds it, G6 now exercises that refusal and the gate's G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning is gone (the conformance run probes the overlay's bound). Decision: fix, pass. Changed: site-limits.example.json (new: an illustrative -10..10 for every control, source operator, labelled example only, not a value of the model); driver.py and facts.md (the statements that a step accepts any control value or that no limit is operator_required); test_driver.py (the cases serve the example overlay; a new case shows the LIMITS_UNSET refusal without it); reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json regenerated. The gate passes G1-G9 with G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND and G8.NO_UNIT x3; the digest changed from sha256:8892dd3b63b24035dd2d1aabf463843c4272ede0fdbd91f56f5d5c11a7916ca1 to sha256:ccf5649d3bdc41eb7ac99d04dbe79d5ecb36092a2b38a72d395de34fdc51c22a because of this intended correction. No source in the clone states a control bound, so none is invented.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review of the reviewer edits made by claude-opus-5-5 with the SDK change MUJOCO-UNBOUNDED-ACTUATORS (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): The model states no actuator control range; the bridge now publishes action.ctrl as operator_required instead of serving it unbounded, so a step that sets it is refused (MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET) until an operator overlay bounds it, and the text that said any value is accepted was corrected. The shipped site-limits.example.json is an example (reason starts 'example only:', issued_by operator:example), not a model bound. Gate passes under collect --strict with the new digest; the only finding change is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE removed. Evidence is contract_checked on the package's fake backend (MuJoCo itself was not run); this is a model review, not a human one.
